test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 19 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Financial inclusion has been a major goal of post-1991 economic reforms in India. Which of the following flagship schemes was launched in 2014 to promote financial inclusion through universal access to banking facilities?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) was launched on **28th August 2014** to promote financial inclusion in India.
 
• The scheme aims to provide **universal access to banking services**, including savings accounts, remittance, credit, insurance, and pension.
 
• Under PMJDY, individuals can open a **zero-balance savings account** with access to a RuPay debit card and accidental insurance cover.
 
• The scheme is an integral part of India's financial inclusion strategy and has resulted in the opening of millions of bank accounts, particularly in rural areas.
 
• PMJDY includes additional benefits such as **overdraft facility of up to ₹10,000** for account holders and direct benefit transfer (DBT) integration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Financial Inclusion**

 
 
• It refers to the process of ensuring access to financial services and adequate credit at affordable costs for all individuals, especially the marginalized and low-income groups.
 
• Financial inclusion helps reduce poverty by enabling people to save, borrow, and invest.
 
 
 
• **RuPay Debit Card**
 
 
• RuPay is India's indigenous payment network developed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).
 
• PMJDY account holders are provided with RuPay debit cards that offer accidental insurance cover.
 
 
 
• **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)**
 
 
• DBT ensures that subsidies and benefits are directly transferred to the bank accounts of beneficiaries.
 
• This reduces leakages and ensures transparency in government schemes.
 
 
 
• **Impact of PMJDY**
 
 
• As of 2023, PMJDY has helped open over 48 crore bank accounts, with a significant proportion in rural areas.
 
• The scheme has facilitated access to formal banking services for millions of previously unbanked individuals.
